through_line: The design idea of a modular, gas-operated, short-stroke piston rifle with ergonomic commonality and parts commonality has survived every revision of the FN SCAR.

stages.title: Initial Concept
stages.summary: The US Special Operations Command (SOCOM) issued a specification for a new family of weapons with ergonomic commonality and parts commonality. FN Herstal began designing the SCAR to meet these requirements.
stages.driver: Combat feedback and the need for a modular rifle system
stages.impact: The SCAR concept was born, aiming to provide a versatile and reliable rifle platform for special operations forces.

changes.detail: allowing for easy caliber changes and configuration

stages.title: Prototype Development
stages.summary: FN Herstal developed the SCAR-L (light) and SCAR-H (heavy) prototypes, chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO and 7.62x51mm NATO, respectively.
stages.driver: The need for a rifle that could adapt to different combat scenarios and environments
stages.impact: The SCAR prototypes demonstrated the potential for a versatile and reliable rifle system.

changes.detail: providing a reliable and durable operating system
allowing operators to switch calibers in the field

stages.title: Trials and Testing
stages.summary: The SCAR prototypes underwent extensive testing and evaluation by SOCOM and other military units.
stages.driver: The need for a rifle that could meet the rigorous demands of special operations forces
stages.impact: The SCAR prototypes demonstrated their reliability, durability, and accuracy in various combat scenarios.

changes.detail: refining the rifle's ergonomics for improved user comfort and handling

stages.title: Initial Fielding
stages.summary: The SCAR was first fielded to US troops in April 2009, with the 75th Ranger Regiment being among the first units to receive the rifle.
stages.driver: The need for a reliable and versatile rifle system for special operations forces
stages.impact: The SCAR was adopted by US special operations forces, providing them with a reliable and adaptable rifle platform.

changes.detail: refining the manufacturing process to improve quality and reduce costs

stages.title: Commercial Variants
stages.summary: FN Herstal introduced the SCAR 16S and SCAR 17S, commercial variants of the SCAR-L and SCAR-H, respectively.
stages.driver: The demand for a civilian version of the SCAR rifle
stages.impact: The SCAR 16S and SCAR 17S provided civilians with access to a reliable and versatile rifle platform.

changes.detail: introducing a new stock design for improved ergonomics and adjustability

stages.title: Next-Generation SCAR
stages.summary: FN Herstal introduced the SCAR Gen 3, featuring improved ergonomics, a new rail system, and enhanced suppressor capability.
stages.driver: The need for a modernized rifle platform that could adapt to evolving combat scenarios and technologies
stages.impact: The SCAR Gen 3 provided users with a refined and improved rifle platform, addressing previous criticisms and limitations.

changes.detail: introducing a new M-LOK rail system for improved accessory mounting and compatibility
refining the rifle's ergonomics for improved user comfort and handling

stages.title: Current Production
stages.summary: The SCAR Gen 3 is currently in production, with FN Herstal continuing to refine and improve the rifle platform.
stages.driver: The ongoing need for a reliable and versatile rifle system for special operations forces and civilian users
stages.impact: The SCAR Gen 3 remains a popular and highly-regarded rifle platform, known for its reliability, durability, and adaptability.

changes.detail: continuously refining the manufacturing process to improve quality and reduce costs
